   @Override

           // or an arguments object. We don't model the arguments object,
           // so let's just be forgiving for now.

   @Override
   public JSType getLeastSupertype(JSType that) {
     // NOTE(nicksantos): When we remove the unknown type, the function types
     // form a lattice with the universal constructor at the top of the lattice,
     // and the NoObject type at the bottom of the lattice.
     //
     // When we introduce the unknown type, it's much more difficult to make
     // heads or tails of the partial ordering of types, because there's no
     // clear hierarchy between the different components (parameter types and
     // return types) in the ArrowType.
     //
     // Rather than make the situation more complicated by introducing new
     // types (like unions of functions), we just fallback on the simpler
     // approach of using the universal constructor and the AnyObject as
     // the supremum and infinum of all function types.
     if (isFunctionType() && that.isFunctionType()) {
       if (equals(that)) {
         return this;
       }
 
       JSType functionInstance = registry.getNativeType(
           JSTypeNative.FUNCTION_INSTANCE_TYPE);
       if (functionInstance.equals(that)) {
         return that;
       } else if (functionInstance.equals(this)) {
         return this;
       }
 
       return registry.getNativeType(JSTypeNative.U2U_CONSTRUCTOR_TYPE);
     }

+package com.fasterxml.jackson.core;
+
+/**
+ * Base class for all exceptions related to processing of JSON content.
+ */
+public abstract class JsonProcessingException extends Exception {
+    private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L;
+
+    protected JsonProcessingException(String msg) {
+        super(msg);
+    }
+
+    protected JsonProcessingException(String msg, Throwable cause) {
+        super(msg, cause);
+    }
+
+    public abstract JsonLocation getLocation();
+}
+
+/**
+ * Exception thrown for cases where JSON processing fails due to coercion issues,
+ * such as overflow when converting a numeric value to a smaller type.
+ */
+public class InputCoercionException extends JsonProcessingException {
+    private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L;
+
+    private final JsonToken inputType;
+    private final Class<?> targetType;
+
+    public InputCoercionException(JsonParser p, String msg, JsonToken inputType, Class<?> targetType) {
+        super(msg, p == null ? null : p.getCurrentLocation());
+        this.inputType = inputType;
+        this.targetType = targetType;
+    }
+
+    public JsonToken getInputType() {
+        return inputType;
+    }
+
+    public Class<?> getTargetType() {
+        return targetType;
+    }
+}

20 ## Abstract Class Mocking
21 Mockito now supports mocking abstract classes. This feature makes it easier to deal with tests that require complex behaviors that are difficult to achieve with traditional mocking techniques.
22 
23 To use abstract class mocking, create an abstract class that implements the interface or class you want to mock. Override the methods you want to provide specific behavior for, and Mockito will instantiate the abstract class for you.
24 
25 For example:
26 
27 ```java
28 abstract class FakeUserAccount implements UserAccount {
29     private final List<String> emails = new ArrayList<>();
30 
31     @Override public void addEmail(String email) {
32         emails.add(email);
33     }
34     @Override List<String> getEmails() {
35         return ImmutableList.copyOf(emails);
36     }
37 }
38 
39 @Fake private FakeUserAccount userAccount; // Mockito instantiates abstract class.
40 ```
41 
42 This feature is particularly useful for testing domain entities, callback-style APIs, and services with uninteresting parameters.
43
